name: vp_ok
description: V. parahaemolyticus O and K antigen loci (OAgc/CPSgc, vpasero)
note: vpautils OAgc.gbk + CPSgc.gbk (Bakta-annotated, MIT), concatenated in source_urls order and built through the cluster pipeline with the committed gapit.typing/2 asset; gene ids resolved at snapshot time (first-use materialization replays the build without re-resolving)

references.citation: van der Graaf-van Bloois L, et al. Kaptive-based O- and K-antigen locus typing of Vibrio parahaemolyticus. Microb Genom 2023;9:mgen001007.
references.note: The OAgc/CPSgc locus references (16 O and 71 K serotypes) that vpautils distributes and this snapshot wraps.

references.citation: indexofire/vpautils: V. parahaemolyticus OAgc.gbk + CPSgc.gbk (MIT, Bakta-annotated).
references.note: The exact committed locus content (MIT), with the typing asset generated by scripts/generate_vp_typing.py.

caveats: O3 and O13 share gene content and cannot be separated from sequence, so the call is the combined label O3/O13 by design.
Variants fold into their base antigen (OL4V1 -> O4, KL20V1 -> K20); untyped OLU*/KLU* loci get no rule and fall back to OUT/KUT, which means 'not in this panel', not 'not typeable'.
Locus matching is Kaptive-style (coverage/identity/key genes), not agglutination; novel or recombinant loci below the 95/95 floors fall back rather than being forced to the nearest type.
The O:K composition is only as good as its ingredients: a KUT fallback yields 'O3:KUT', which names the O antigen and states that the K antigen is unresolved.
